s1.syndrome_frame: Painless swelling in the supraclavicular region with gradual enlargement over six years
salient_findings: 4.0-cm diameter, round, firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area
Ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
key_facts: 32-year-old man
Six-year history of painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region
Swelling gradually enlarged from the size of an almond to that of a lime
No history of trauma, fever, or systemic illness
No weakness, numbness, or loss of function in the upper limb
Mass is 4.0-cm in diameter and round
Mass is firm and non-tender
Mobile in the medio-lateral direction
Ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass
Mass has well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
Lower border of the mass lies adjacent to the subclavian artery
Medial border of the mass abuts the carotid artery and external jugular vein

shortlist.label: Branchial cleft cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound and cystogram findings corroborate this diagnosis, and the mass's characteristics (superficial, heterogeneous, round, cystic, well-defined smooth margins, multiple intralesional septa) are consistent with a branchial cleft cyst.

shortlist.label: Cystic lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: The mass's cystic nature and location in the supraclavicular region could be consistent with a cystic lymphangioma, although the ultrasound findings and clinical presentation are more suggestive of a branchial cleft cyst.

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: The firm, non-tender mass in the supraclavicular region could be a schwannoma, but the ultrasound findings of a heterogeneous, cystic mass with multiple intralesional septa are less typical for this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, lymphoma could present as a painless swelling in the supraclavicular region, and the patient's age and lack of systemic symptoms do not rule out this diagnosis entirely.

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: A lipoma could present as a firm, non-tender mass in the supraclavicular region, but the ultrasound findings of a heterogeneous, cystic mass with multiple intralesional septa are not typical for a lipoma.

raw.rationale: The ultrasound findings of a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa, along with the cystogram findings, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cystic lymphangioma
rejected.why: While possible, the location and ultrasound characteristics are more typical of a branchial cleft cyst.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid, not cystic, and do not usually have the same ultrasound characteristics.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would likely present with systemic symptoms and multiple lymph node involvement, not a single, slowly enlarging mass.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically homogeneous and do not have the cystic, septated appearance seen on ultrasound in this case.
